tags.name: Cali Ship Wreck
tags.qa_notes: 2026-07-22 re-audit: depth (2.7-9m) and history re-confirmed via fresh search (underanendlesssky.com, caymancompass.com, amusingplanet.com). Length discrepancy (206ft vs 220ft) still present across sources and remains flagged rather than resolved. No factual corrections needed from 2026-05-20 pass.

tags.name: USS Kittiwake Shipwreck
tags.qa_notes: 2026-07-22 re-audit CORRECTION: the 2026-05-20 pass's 'flight data recorder' claim was itself wrong. Cross-checked against Wikipedia and Divetech's dedicated debunking article (which cites official Navy salvage-log contact records): the Space Shuttle Challenger did not carry a flight data recorder/black box at all — the crew compartment recorder was recovered by USS Preserver, a different vessel. Kittiwake's actual, source-confirmed role was recovering a Solid Rocket Booster (SRB) segment from ~175-177 ft during the Feb-Aug 1986 salvage operation. Markdown corrected accordingly. Length 251ft confirmed; displacement reported as 1,780 tons standard (some sources give ~2,045 tons full load — noted as a range, not a single figure). Tropical Storm Nate (Oct 2017) cause of port-side tipping reconfirmed.

2026-07-22 re-audit: ~100 individuals reconfirmed via Guy Harvey Foundation's long-running stingray survey (DoE data, 'broadly stable... around one hundred individuals over the last decade'). Wingspan claim tightened — sources give a range (up to ~1.5m/5ft for females per some sources, up to ~2m per others), so markdown now cites a range rather than a single 'exceeding 1.5m' figure. Population/depth/species corrections from 2026-05-20 pass hold.

2026-07-22 re-audit CORRECTION: the wall's total drop depth is disputed across independent sources — figures found range from ~1,000ft to 6,000+ft (and one source converts to ~2,000m). The 2026-05-20 markdown's single '6,000 feet' figure has been softened to reflect this spread rather than asserting one number. Wall start depth (~5-6m) and Nassau grouper habituation reconfirmed.

2026-07-22 re-audit CORRECTION: silverside season timing conflicts across sources — the 2026-05-20 pass asserted 'August-September' as confirmed, but fresh sources (divephotoguide.com, jetsetjansen.com, theresidencesgrandcaymanrentals.com) describe June through early August. Markdown now flags this as a genuine source conflict rather than a single confirmed window. Depth (~15m) and shore-entry location reconfirmed.

2026-07-22 re-audit: re-fetched oceanfrontiers.com directly — confirms pinnacle top 45ft/base 100ft+, but the operator's own page does not name specific species (only 'abundant marine life'). A third-party aggregator mentioned 'hammerhead shark' at this site but this is NOT corroborated by the primary operator source, so it was not added — avoiding an unconfirmed rare-species claim. Chromis/barracuda/parrotfish/angelfish attribution downgraded to 'commonly reported' rather than operator-confirmed since the current Ocean Frontiers page text doesn't itemize them; other sources (PADI, Tortuga Divers) still support these species generally for the site.

2026-07-22 re-audit: pinnacle top (~15m/50ft) and the 33m/110ft hole ('do not swim through') reconfirmed via CITA Dive 365 listing and additional dive-site aggregators. West Bay/North Wall location (not Little Cayman) reconfirmed. No further corrections needed from 2026-05-20 pass.
2026-07-22 re-audit: exit depth (~30m/100ft), Northwest Point location, current-prone difficulty, and blacktip/Caribbean reef shark presence all reconfirmed via fresh search. No corrections needed.

2026-07-22 re-audit: length (375ft) and tonnage (1,389 gross tons) now independently cross-confirmed (previously length was cited but tonnage only came from one source lineage; a fresh NUMA/general search independently corroborates both figures). Depth reported across sources as 25-40ft (7.6-12.2m) rather than a flat 8-10m — markdown widened to 8-12m to reflect the range. 1932 hurricane sinking and 1957 dynamiting reconfirmed. A single-source anecdote (captain's strongbox funding a waterfront church) was found but not corroborated elsewhere, so it was NOT added per the 2+ source rule for historical claims.

2026-07-22 re-audit: repeated the search with fresh queries and fetched two additional South Side wall-list pages (walltowalldiving.com top-10 list, caymanturtledivers.com wall list) — neither names 'Chinese Wall' specifically. Still no 3rd independent site-specific source found. Left validated=false per policy rather than padding with weak sources. Flagged as unresolved in this QA pass.

2026-07-22 re-audit: depth (avg ~16m/52ft, max ~30m/98ft) and eagle ray aggregation behavior reconfirmed and expanded with a 4th independent source (Living the Dream Divers dive log) — rays reported in groups of 2-6 typically, with occasional counts up to ~20 in spring/summer. Cleaning stations, lobster, moray eels reconfirmed. Caribbean reef sharks remain unconfirmed as regular residents.

2026-07-22 re-audit: found one genuinely site-specific quote — caymanturtledivers.com calls Japanese Gardens 'a naturally occurring interactive museum' — added to markdown with attribution. Checked additional South Side/hidden-site lists (redsailcayman.com hidden sites, indigodivers.com) — neither names Japanese Garden. Still only 1 true site-specific source plus 2 regional-only sources, short of the 3-independent-source bar, so validated remains false.

2026-07-22 re-audit: Japanese cable-laying ship, ~70-80ft length, 1981 sinking (yachtscaymans.com independently states 1981, consistent with existing 1981/1982 split), and Doc Poulson namesake story all reconfirmed via a 4th independent source. Depth (~50-60ft/15-18m) reconfirmed. No corrections needed from 2026-05-20 pass.

2026-07-22 re-audit: 330ft length, Koni II class, 1984 Soviet build for Cuban Navy, and 1996 scuttling reconfirmed via a 5th independent source (military-history.fandom.com Koni-class reference + Cayman Marl Road). Hurricane Ivan 2004 hull break reconfirmed by freedomtourtravel.com directly. Tonnage/displacement is NOT stated in markdown because Koni-class sources disagree materially (standard displacement reported anywhere from ~1,140 to ~1,463 tons, full load ~1,900-1,930 tons, depending on variant) and no source gives a hull-specific figure for this ship — omitted rather than guessed, per policy. Refined 'Legislative Assembly' service description: Cayman Compass/Marl Road indicate the 23 years of public service spanned the Assembly of Justices and Vestry (1946-62) plus two later Legislative Assembly terms (1965-68, 1976-80), not one continuous Legislative Assembly tenure — markdown corrected.

2026-07-22 re-audit CORRECTION: the 'notable appearance in the film' claim was overstated. Fresh research (movie-locations.com, subslikescript.com script excerpt) shows Trinity Caves is referenced BY NAME in The Firm's dialogue/script ('My friends are taking him to Trinity Caves...') but sources conflict on whether underwater footage was actually filmed there or the site was merely name-dropped. Markdown softened to reflect this. Three converging coral canyons (not true caves), tarpon/lobster/reef fish reconfirmed.

2026-07-22 re-audit: Three Fathom Wall alias, ~18ft (5.5m) start depth, and Bloody Bay Wall/Jackson Bight junction reconfirmed via fresh search (Tripadvisor reviews, greatestdivesites.com). Marine life list reconfirmed as site-specific by Little Cayman Divers and greatestdivesites.com. No corrections needed.
